//: Machine-local overrides for the deliver/pr-* skill family. Copy to ~/.agents/local/config.json and fill in. Never commit the filled-in copy: it names private repos, hosts and bot accounts.
//protected_branches_extra: Branch patterns that are ALSO protected, on top of the built-in main, master and stage-*. Entries are glob patterns: a bare name matches exactly, * matches any run of characters, so "rc-*" covers every dated release candidate. Used by deliver, pr-open, pr-babysit, pr-merge.
//pr_review_default_repo: owner/repo that pr-review targets when the cwd has no useful origin remote. Omit to always derive from git remote get-url origin.
//rebase_sync_repos: owner/repo entries whose CLAUDE.md mandates rebase-before-push. For these, pr-babysit/pr-merge rebase onto the target and force-push with --force-with-lease instead of merging forward.
//ai_reviewer_usernames_gitlab: GitLab usernames of AI reviewers, added to the built-in list. Comments from these are auto-addressed; everything else batches as human.
//ai_reviewer_usernames_github: GitHub usernames of AI reviewers, added to the built-in ["cursor"]. The [bot] suffix is stripped before matching.
//sonar_host_url: SonarQube base URL. Omit or leave empty to skip the SonarQube phase entirely.
//bot_noise_body_markers_extra: Extra HTML-comment markers that identify a bot comment as noise, added to the built-in list.
//personal_backlog: Where post-merge-cleanup writes a deferred item that doesn't warrant a tracker ticket. Not per-repo — it's your backlog, wherever you keep it. Configure the app/destination its connector needs; that destination is then the source of truth, so nothing is also written locally to drift from it. Unset, or its connector missing this session, falls back to a local markdown note.

personal_backlog.page_url: <url of the page to append to>
personal_backlog.page_id: <its id, if the connector needs one>
personal_backlog.fallback: <what to do when the connector is unavailable>
personal_backlog.layout: <where a new entry goes, and how a finished one is marked done>

//auto_approval: Per-repo, keyed by 'github/<owner>/<repo>'. A repo where applying a label requests an automated review. pr-open adds it after opening when the diff meets opt_in_criterion. label: the label to add. mechanism: how it is triggered, for the report. opt_in / opt_in_criterion: when it applies and the test a diff must meet. notes: traps worth remembering. Applying it only requests a review — the bot triages risk itself and declines what it does not like — so it needs no approval gate. Omit a repo and pr-open never labels it.
//review_request_mechanism: How pr-open Step 7 asks for review. 'github-reviewers' proposes reviewers on the PR itself and skips Slack, since pinging as well splits the thread. Unset means a Slack draft via voice.
//review_request_channel: Slack channel the Step 7 draft is addressed to, when Slack is the mechanism.
//review_request_handle: Group handle to open that draft with. Preferred over naming individuals — it reaches whoever is free, which is how a claim-by-reaction channel works. Unset falls back to whoever Luis names, else an @<reviewer> placeholder.
//second_opinion_review: Per-repo, keyed by 'github/<owner>/<repo>'. Turns on a second correctness pass by a different model: self-review Step 3.6 on your own diff, pr-review Step 3.5 on someone else's PR. Omit a repo and the step never runs there, unless the map has a '*' entry: the machine-wide fallback, used by any repo without an entry of its own. Set a repo's entry to false to keep it off. It is opt-in because the reviewer is handed your diff, and where that goes is a per-codebase decision, so add '*' only on a machine where every repo you'd clone may go to that vendor (a work laptop under an enterprise agreement, say). command: a non-interactive CLI taking instructions as an argument and reading content on stdin. It is run from a scratch directory, not the repo, so include whatever flag that CLI needs to accept a non-repo working directory (codex needs --skip-git-repo-check). Pin the model and reasoning effort in it too (codex: -m <model> -c model_reasoning_effort=<level>): left bare it runs whatever the CLI defaults to, which for codex was its frontier model at no reasoning at all. Pin the newest generation of a model rather than a previous one. max_rounds: how many times the convergence loop may re-run it after fixes (2 is usually enough; the cap exists because a second model will always find something on a large diff). notes: traps worth remembering.
//staging_verification: Per-repo, keyed by 'github/<owner>/<repo>'. Enables deliver's B5 staging-verification phase for repos that gate deploys on manual testing. Omit a repo and the phase never runs for it. needs_testing_label: the PR label that marks a change as needing post-deploy testing. staging_url: the deployed environment to drive. deploy_state_cmd: a command that reports whether a given sha has landed on each surface. notes: free-text traps worth remembering, appended as they cost time.

github/acme-org/example-repo.deploy_state_cmd: <command taking a sha, reporting deployed/not per surface>

//local_e2e: Per-repo, keyed the same way. Read by self-review Step 3.5 before driving the app locally. start: how to bring the stack up. app_url: where it lands. login: how to authenticate a test user. notes: traps that have cost time before — append rather than rediscover.

github/acme-org/example-repo.start: <command that brings the local stack up>

//project_context: Maps a tracker project to the one page holding its engineering background, read by understand-task and deliver. Keyed by '<tracker>:<project id>': a Linear project, a Jira epic, whatever the tracker groups tickets by; ids rather than names, which change. The value is the page's URL, wherever it lives (Notion, Linear, Drive, a Slack canvas), or null for a project known to have none, so it isn't asked about again. understand-task adds an entry when it asks about a project it hasn't seen.
//verification_addenda: Extra verification commands for repos whose nested apps own a separate pipeline. Run by self-review and pr-merge when a changed path starts with when_paths_under.

verification_addenda.run: cd apps/example && pnpm install && pnpm lint && pnpm test && pnpm build
